Inverse of \(3\) modulo \(25\) is \(17\), so
\[
3x \equiv 1 \pmod{25} \implies x \equiv 17 \pmod{25}.
\]
Thus we combine:
\[
x \equiv 3 \pmod 2,\quad x \equiv 6 \pmod 9,\quad x \equiv 17 \pmod{25}.
\]
First two give:
\[
x=9k+6,\quad 9k+6\equiv 3 \pmod 2 \implies k\equiv 1 \pmod 2,
\]
so \(k=2t+1\), hence
\[
x=18t+15 \implies x\equiv 15 \pmod{18}.
\]
Now combine with \(x\equiv 17\pmod{25}\):
\[
18t+15\equiv 17 \pmod{25}
\]
\[
18t\equiv 2 \pmod{25}.
\]
Since \(18^{-1}\equiv 7\pmod{25}\),
\[
t\equiv 14\pmod{25}.
\]
So
\[
x=18(25s+14)+15=450s+267.
\]
The least positive four-digit solution is when \(s=2\):
\[
x=450(2)+267=1167.
\]

\[
\boxed{1167}
\]
